conjecture: Dominance-Support (DS) conjecture for Hikita's ⋆-product: for any partition λ, e_λ^{(q,t)}(X) := e_{λ_1}⋆⋯⋆e_{λ_l} lies in span_{ℚ(q,t)}{e_μ(X) : μ ≥ λ in dominance order}. Sharpened DS-triangular form: leading coefficient of e_λ is q^{-n(λ)} where n(λ) = Σ (i-1)λ_i (Macdonald n-statistic), and all other coefficients c_{λμ}(q,t) vanish at q=1. SP (Day 195 conjecture) is the length-2 slice of DS. Verified 22-for-22 in Day 196 (length 1 trivial; length 2 = Day 195's 18 cases; length 3 = 3 new cases (2,1,1), (3,1,1), (2,2,1); length 4 = 2 new cases (1,1,1,1), (2,1,1,1)).

tree.approach: Dominance-Support: e_λ^{(q,t)} = q^{-n(λ)} e_λ + Σ_{μ ≻ λ} c_{λμ}(q,t) e_μ, with c_{λμ}(1,t) = 0. Empirically 22-for-22. Implies SP (length-2 slice). Implies meta-conjecture min(a,b)+1 for length-2. Suggests Macdonald-triangularity connection.
tree.recheck: 2026-09-16 empirical tests at length 3 and 4 across 5 new cases; leading coefficient q^{-n(λ)} verified.

Tested λ = (2,1,1), (3,1,1), (2,2,1) at m=5,6. DS holds; leading coefficient q^{-n(λ)} = q^{-3}, q^{-3}, q^{-4} respectively (matches formula).

τ_r(q,t) · q³ = A(q,t) + B(q,t)·t^r + C(q,t)·t^(2r), with A = −(q²−1)(q−t−1)/(t²−1), B = t(q²−1)(q−t)/(t−1), C = −q·t³·(q²−1)/(t²−1). Fit r=2,3,4 verified r=5,6. Rule 11 fire #25 (three-monomial unfold).

If such an identification works, DS follows from classical Macdonald triangularity.

Route 2c: identify D_{(a)} from D'Adderio-Interdonato-Iraci-Pagaria arXiv 2608.14836 with e_a(Y) action in Hikita level-1 rep. If YES, D'Adderio's linear-time formula gives the operator-level closed form and DS + Pieri closed forms drop out analytically for all a.
children.reason: Direct SymPy test at m=3,r=1 and m=4,r=2: D_{(2)} e_r in p-basis differs structurally from e_2⋆e_r. Specifically the p_(4) coefficient of D_{(2)} e_2 is identically zero, whereas Hikita's e_2⋆e_2 has p_(4) coefficient = -(q-1)(t²+1)(qt²+qt+q-t)/(4q²) ≠ 0. No monomial q^i t^j rescaling can bridge nonzero → zero. At q=1, D_{(2)} f = h_2 · f (verified via p_(1,1,1,1) − p_(2,2))/4 = h_2·e_2), so D_{(a)} is the h-side Pieri, while Hikita's e_a⋆ is the e-side. Different Pieri families.

children.approach: Rescue hypothesis: D_{(a)} = h_a ⋆_Hikita, i.e. multiplication by h_a(Y) in Hikita's level-1 rep. Tested at (a,r,m) = (2,1,3), (2,2,4), raw and under every monomial q^i t^j rescaling.
children.reason: Match table 0/3 at (2,1,3) and 0/5 at (2,2,4) raw; renormalization sweep produces irreducible non-monomial rational-function ratios like -q^3(t-1)/((q^2-qt-1)(t^2+t+1)); no monomial rescaling closes them. Diagnostic: at q=1, D_{(2)} e_r DOES equal ordinary h_2·e_r, but h_2(Y).e_r at q=1 does NOT equal h_2·e_r. Conclusion: the Y-generated symmetric-function action is intrinsically e-side; the map Λ → End(Λ_m), f ↦ f(Y_1,...,Y_m), is not a ring homomorphism into ordinary Λ-multiplication under any Newton-induced identification. Cannot manufacture h-side Pieri from Y-operators.
